problem: The parenthetical "(and repeats at a repeated point)" is wrong for inner control points. Repeating an inner control point P1 = P2 does not make the curve pass through that point; at t = 0.5, for example, the curve point is (1/8)P0 + (3/4)P1 + (1/8)P3, which is generally not P1. A student will take away the false rule that repeating a control point puts the curve on it.
fix: Write: "A Bezier curve interpolates only its two end points. A repeated end point (P0 = P1) only makes the start tangent zero; it does not create a new interpolation point, and repeating an inner point does not make the curve pass through it."

problem: The symbol Pi(1) for the interpolated point of the first de Casteljau level is ambiguous: it reads like point Pi with an argument, not a superscript level index. Students may confuse it with the parameter t or with a power.
fix: Write P<sub>i</sub><sup>(1)</sup> = (1−t)P<sub>i</sub> + tP<sub>i+1</sub>, and say that the superscript (1) is the level number, not an exponent.
